tools.name: summarize_meeting
tools.description: Generate an AI summary of a recorded meeting using one of the backend's sales-qualification templates, and store it on the meeting. Pass the meeting id and a `type` from get_meeting_summary_types; the transcript, participants and existing summaries are read from the meeting automatically. Can take up to 3 minutes: it runs a full LLM generation over the transcript. If the meeting ended within the last 48 hours and its recap email has not been sent, storing the summary also sends that email to the recipients the project's meeting settings name (notesSending).

type.description: Summary template to generate — a `type` value from get_meeting_summary_types (e.g. general, bant, meddic, deal_intelligence). Any casing is accepted.

sections.description: JSON array of sections to produce, to narrow the template. Omit to use the template's own backend-defined sections (the normal case).

tools.name: expand_meeting_summary_element
tools.description: Elaborate one item of a meeting's existing AI summary (console's per-bullet "Expand by AI"). Requires a summary to already exist — run summarize_meeting first. Identify the item by its summary `type`, the `sectionName` it sits in, and the `element` itself, all readable from get_meeting's summary value. The elaborated item replaces the original in the stored summary.

type.description: Which existing summary to expand within — a key of get_meeting's `summary` value (lowercase, e.g. general). Any casing is accepted.

sectionName.description: Name of the section containing the item, as it appears in that summary

element.description: The summary item to expand, as JSON, copied whole from that section (its `start` is how the server finds it)

tools.name: update_meeting
tools.description: Change a meeting's own fields: title, description, location, notes, or any other attribute by name. At least one field is required; unnamed fields keep their values. Read the current values with get_meeting first.

notes.description: The meeting's notes as a JSON array of {start, type, text} objects, replacing the current notes. Copy the array from get_meeting's `notes` value and edit it.

attributeValues.description: JSON object of any other attribute to set, keyed by its column name from list_meeting_attributes.

tools.name: relabel_meeting_transcript_speakers
tools.description: Rename speakers in a meeting transcript — replaces the diarizer's generic labels with real names. Improves every summary generated afterwards, so it is worth doing before summarize_meeting on a transcript full of "Speaker 1"-style labels. The meeting's existing summaries are regenerated in the background with the new names. Renaming back with the reverse map restores the labels, unless two labels were mapped to the same name.

nameMap.description: JSON object mapping each current speaker label to its real name, e.g. {"Speaker 1": "Ada Lovelace"}

instructions:
Intempt platform access: 50 tools over a customer-data platform (segments, events, users/accounts, journeys, experiences, analytics reports, meetings, brand/designer assets, and AI content generation).

CAPABILITIES: 27 read, 5 single-record edit, 12 multi-view, and 6 session/auth/content-generation tools. It cannot create entities or run bulk operations -- no such tool is served, so if a user asks for one, say so plainly and point them at the Intempt console rather than approximating it with a sequence of edits. No delete tool is served in the current tool set.

SCOPE: every data call runs against one organization + project. Check with 'whoami'. Switch with 'use_project' -- it takes effect on the next call, with no restart. 'list_orgs' / 'list_projects' enumerate what the user may reach. If a call fails with "No organization or project selected", the user belongs to several orgs and none is selected yet: call 'use_project', do not guess one. A failure saying "Not logged in" is a DIFFERENT problem -- call 'login' and do not offer to set environment variables.

⚠️ SWITCHING PROJECT CHANGES WHAT WRITES TOUCH. The content-generation tools ('generate_*') persist a real record into the ACTIVE project. Confirm the scope before generating into a project the user has just switched to.

RESPONSE SHAPE: collections are capped and projected to fit the transport, so a response can be complete-looking yet partial. Two keys tell you when:
  _truncated -- items were cut. It reports the true total and names the exact 'offset' to pass for the next page. Page with 'offset' rather than telling the user the list is short.
  _shaped -- per-item FIELDS were dropped to fit a size budget. The records are all there; some attributes are not. Re-read one record with its detail tool ('get_*') to see everything.
Never report a capped count as the total -- read _truncated.total instead.

SEARCH CAVEAT: the searchTerm on 'list_users' and 'list_segment_users' cannot match a value containing "@" -- a confirmed backend encoding bug, and both tools POST the same endpoint. Searching by email address returns nothing, which does NOT mean the user is absent. Filter by name, or page with pageNumber/perPage.

SEGMENT MEMBERSHIP: to answer "who is in segment X", call 'list_segments' for the id, then 'list_segment_users' with that segmentId. Do NOT try to filter 'list_users' by segment -- it takes no segment argument and would return the whole project.

ATTRIBUTE COLUMNS: 'list_users' and 'list_segment_users' return ONLY identity markers unless you pass 'columns'. A missing field means you did not ask for it -- NOT that the user has no value. Call 'list_attribute_columns' first; its ids are project-specific, so never reuse ids from another project.
